title: Security posture discovery - Acme Bio internal review

Agreed to follow up with SOC2 report, architecture diagram for Private deployment, and a deeper technical deep-dive with platform engineers next week.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-12 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Meyer (Redwood SE), Lindsey Cho (Redwood CSM), Alex Chen (Acme InfoSec), Priya Kapoor (Acme Platform), Sam Torres (Acme CTO), Diego Ramos (Acme Procurement)

---- Auto-generated summary (may be imprecise) ----
Maya: quick intro, agenda to cover compliance artifacts, SSO, KMS, logs, and deployment options.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, uh thanks for carving time. I'm Maya Patel, lead AE on the account at Redwood, and with me is Jonas Meyer, our solutions engineer. Could each of you give a 1-liner on role?
[00:12] Alex: Alex Chen, I run InfoSec at Acme Bio, focusing on compliance and risk assessments.
[00:16] Priya: Priya Kapoor, platform eng, I own onboarding and infra integrations.
[00:21] Sam: Sam Torres, CTO, here to make sure we can move fast but keep data private.
[00:26] Diego: Diego Ramos, procurement, listening for budget/timelines.
[00:30] Jonas: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO posture, SSO and identity, RBAC model, audit logs & retention, encryption and KMS, then deployment options - hosted vs dedicated vs private. Sound good?
[00:45] Alex: Yep. First thing: do you have a SOC 2 Type II right now? And ISO 27001? That's biggest gating factor for us.
[00:53] Maya: Yes, we maintain SOC 2 Type II across our hosted control plane — we can share the report. Regarding ISO, we have an in-progress ISO 27001 program; we do not currently hold a certificate but we can share our risk register and the controls mapping.
[01:07] Alex: Okay. If we go hosted we need to know what data is stored in logs and for how long. We can't have PHI/sequence-level data retained longer than 90 days in logs in EU regions.
[01:21] Jonas: Understood. For hosted we have configurable log retention; default is 30 days, can be extended to 90 or more. For audit logs — we capture request/response metadata, not full PII by default, but if you choose to store transcripts we can enable or disable. Note: auto-transcript capture sometimes picks up model outputs, so you'd want to opt-out if that's a no-go.
[01:43] Priya: Can you do VPC peering or private link to avoid internet egress for calls? Our policy requires no data plane traffic traversing the public internet for EU workloads.
[01:57] Jonas: Yes — Dedicated and Private options support VPC peering and PrivateLink. For Private deployment we can do a customer-controlled VPC with a private control plane, or an on-prem bundle if you need air-gapped. There's some setup overhead but it's supported.
[02:13] Sam: What's the difference operationally between Dedicated and Private? I want to understand encryption key control and who holds keys.
[02:22] Maya: Good question. Dedicated is isolated GPU pools in our infra but keys are still managed by Redwood by default. We offer customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS for Dedicated in our enterprise plan. Private gives you the option to bring-your-own-key in your own KMS/HSM in your VPC — full control. We can rotate keys per your schedule.
[02:38] Alex: Is HSM required for us to attest? We need proof of key custody separation in audits.
[02:44] Jonas: We support HSM-backed CMKs via AWS KMS and can integrate with external HSM through our Private deployment. We can provide the key custody diagrams for auditors.
[02:54] Diego: From procurement, can we get a redacted SOC2 report and a data processing addendum? Also, what about subprocessor list?
[03:03] Maya: Absolutely — we'll send a redacted SOC2 Type II, a DPA template, and our subprocessors list. Expect to receive those in the follow-up email.
[03:12] Alex: What about SSO? We use Okta and some teams use Azure AD, SAML only. Do you support SCIM for provisioning?
[03:21] Jonas: We support SSO via SAML 2.0 with Okta and Azure AD. SCIM provisioning is available for enterprise accounts — we can push users and groups and sync group membership for RBAC.
[03:30] Priya: RBAC — we need fine-grained roles: admin, viewer, engineer, app-integrations only, plus token scoping for model access. How granular can you get?
[03:39] Maya: Our RBAC supports custom roles beyond basic admin/viewer: you can scope API keys to routes (embeddings vs generation), pin to models, and set rate limits. For intense least-privilege use cases we usually implement token scoping combined with SCIM-managed groups.
[03:52] Alex: Are audit logs immutable? We require tamper-evidence for logs for at least 2 years for certain projects.
[03:59] Jonas: Audit logs are append-only in our system and we can export them to your S3/Azure storage for long-term retention. We also publish signed digests to demonstrate integrity; that said, the retention windows need to be configured explicitly.
[04:13] Sam: On encryption in transit — TLS 1.2 minimum? Any mutual TLS options?
[04:20] Jonas: We require TLS 1.2+ in transit, and mutual TLS is available in Private deployments and as an option for Dedicated. Hosted API supports standard TLS with API key auth and optional mTLS with enterprise onboarding.
[04:33] Priya: For data residency, can you pin to eu-west-1 and ensure logs and model state live only in that region?
[04:41] Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can request region-restricted deployments for enterprise, we need to confirm availability in specific regions though.
[04:52] Alex: What's your policy on model caching/KV cache? Because some of our outputs could be considered derived PHI if we cache prefixes.
[05:01] Jonas: Good callout. Our runtime has a KV cache for prefix reuse to reduce latency and cost. We can disable KV cache for your tenant or mark certain prompts non-cacheable. The default is workload-aware caching, but for sensitive workloads we recommend disabling or using private deployments. Note: transcription auto-caching sometimes stores small context; we'll show how to disable that in the deep-dive.
[05:20] Priya: Do you support customer-controlled log export to our SIEM (Splunk) with signed delivery?
[05:27] Jonas: Yes — we can push audit logs and telemetry to your SIEM via secure delivery channels; we support S3 pushes with encryption and HTTP endpoints with auth, plus a signed manifest for each export.
[05:37] Alex: On the ISO front, you said in-progress. Do you have compensating controls mapped to ISO 27001 Annex A yet?
[05:45] Maya: We have a controls mapping doc — we'll include it. It's one of the things we've shared with customers going through vendor risk assessments.
[05:52] Diego: Timeline question: if we choose Dedicated, how long from contract to live?
[05:58] Jonas: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 6-8 weeks depending on requirements (network setup, KMS integration, SOC/contract review). Private installs or on-prem can be longer, 8-12 weeks.
[06:10] Sam: For billing and invoicing, do you need a PO upfront?
[06:13] Maya: Procurement configurable — for committed Dedicated we do monthly/annual invoicing and accept POs. We'll coordinate terms with Diego.
[06:20] Alex: A few technical nitpicks: how do you handle retention for model artifacts—like intermediate KV cache, embeddings stored for search indexes — are those considered customer data?
[06:31] Jonas: Embeddings and vector indexes are customer data. For Hosted we allow either Redwood-managed vector store or customer-managed via connectors to your VPC. Retention of embeddings is configurable; for strict cases we recommend customer-managed vector store with local encryption keys.
[06:46] Priya: If we do Private, can we use our own HSM over the network? We have a Thales HSM cluster in our VPC.
[06:53] Jonas: Yes, Private supports integrating with external HSMs over private network links; we can provide the handshake and key wrapping docs. There are a few latency considerations but it's doable.
[07:04] Alex: Regarding logging of prompts/outputs — can you redact or mask PII or PHI before logs are stored?
[07:12] Jonas: We offer configurable redaction rules and an SDK pre-hook that can remove or hash fields before they're sent. For hosted quickstarts we also provide a managed redaction service, but for highest assurance we recommend pre-processing client-side.
[07:26] Maya: Quick clarification on audits: we'll provide SOC 2 Type II, pen test summary, subprocessors, DPA. For ISO we can provide our controls mapping and roadmap.
[07:36] Alex: Good. Do you do third-party pen tests annually?
[07:40] Jonas: Yes, we do yearly penetration tests and vulnerability scans; results are summarized in the pen test summary we share with NDA when necessary.
[07:48] Diego: Anything we need from procurement side to expedite? Contracts template?
[07:52] Maya: We'll send a standard SOW + MSA template and pricing worksheet. Diego, if you can share procurement terms (net30/45 etc.) we'll align.
[07:59] Sam: For the pilot, we'd want a bounded POC — maybe 3 nodes dedicated, region EU - what's your recommended pilot config?
[08:07] Jonas: For evaluation, we typically recommend a small dedicated pool (2-4 GPUs) with logging turned off or exported to your S3, plus private key integration if you want to validate KMS flows. That gives you throughput numbers and latency tails without full production provisioning.
[08:22] Priya: Security-specific: do you support org-level SAML + per-project RBAC? We want central SSO but project-level isolation.
[08:31] Maya: Yes — org-level SAML + SCIM group sync works with per-project RBAC scoping. We'll show a sample mapping in the deep-dive.
[08:40] Alex: Audit trail requirements: we need user-level actions with IP, timestamp, API key used, and a digest proving immutability. Can Redwood provide all of that?
[08:51] Jonas: Yes, the audit schema includes user, IP, timestamp, request id, and action. We can produce signed digests for immutability and export them.
[09:00] Alex: Any complications with GDPR when you export logs to our S3 in EU?
[09:05] Jonas: If logs remain in EU regions and we don't transfer them outside, GDPR requirements are met. For Hosted with region pinning, we ensure storage doesn't leave the jurisdiction. For Dedicated/Private it's straightforward since resources live in your VPC/region.
[09:17] Maya: Okay lets move toward next steps: we'll send the SOC2, DPA, subprocessors list, and a Private architecture diagram. We'll also schedule a technical deep-dive with Jonas and Priya next week.
[09:30] Priya: Sounds good. One more: does Redwood support data deletion requests and a documented process for erasure?
[09:37] Jonas: Yes — we have documented data deletion APIs and procedures. For Hosted we can bulk-delete customer artifacts; for Private you'd control deletion in your environment. We'll attach the deletion SLA to the DPA.
[09:49] Alex: Last check: who signs the DPA and can you accept customer-specific clauses around liability?
[09:55] Maya: We can negotiate specific DPA clauses; standard process is to iterate on DPA and legal will review. Large customers often have a limited set of exceptions we accept.
[10:05] Diego: Great. If you can get the artifacts by Friday, procurement will start the internal review.
[10:10] Maya: We'll aim for that. Any final questions?
[10:16] Sam: No, thanks — let's get that SOC2 and schedule the deep-dive.
[10:20] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the email and calendar invites.

---- End transcript ----
notes: Typical sales-security discovery with emphasis on SOC2, KMS, HSM, SSO/SCIM, RBAC, log immutability, and deployment options. Customer leans toward Dedicated/Private due to PHI risk; agreed next steps and deliverables.
